name: PostHog
description: PostHog is a product intelligence platform that combines product analytics, web analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, and a customer data pipeline so teams can understand and improve user behavior.
best_for: Product teams and developers at companies of any size wanting analytics, experimentation, and data infrastructure in one platform, with SDKs for Next.js, React, Python, and 20+ other frameworks/languages.
features: Feature flags and no-code A/B testing experiments
Error tracking and AI observability (traces and logs)
Customer data platform (CDP) for routing event data to other tools
Managed data warehouse for querying product data

alternatives.name: Amplitude
alternatives.description: A product analytics platform combining analytics, feedback, experimentation, and feature management.
alternatives.best_for: Product, data, and engineering teams needing analytics with feature experimentation.

alternatives.name: Mixpanel
alternatives.description: A product intelligence platform combining analytics, session replay, experiments, and AI-powered insights.
alternatives.best_for: Product, data, and engineering teams wanting fast, data-driven product decisions.

alternatives.name: Segment
alternatives.description: Twilio's customer data platform for collecting, unifying, and activating first-party customer data.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations that primarily need a data pipeline to unify and route customer data across many tools.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Resets every month, forever; no credit card required. Includes 1M product-analytics events, 5K session recordings, 1M feature-flag requests, 100K error-tracking exceptions, 1,500 survey responses, 1M data-warehouse rows, 10GB logs ingested, plus smaller allowances for AI/other products.

tiers.name: Pay-as-you-go — Product Analytics (per event, after 1M free events/mo)
tiers.notes: Step-down usage pricing confirmed on posthog.com/docs/product-analytics/pricing: $0.0000500/event (1-2M), $0.0000343/event (2-15M), $0.0000295/event (15-50M), $0.0000218/event (50-100M), $0.0000150/event (100-250M), $0.0000090/event (250M+). Other products (session replay, feature flags, error tracking, surveys, etc.) are metered and billed separately by their own unit. No per-seat charge on any plan — team members are unlimited.

tiers.name: Boost (platform package, optional flat add-on)
tiers.notes: Confirmed on posthog.com/platform-packages. Adds unlimited projects, white labeling, HIPAA BAA, SSO enforcement, 2FA requirement. Activity-log retention only 7 days; session-replay retention 12 months; no stated priority-support SLA.

tiers.name: Scale (platform package, optional flat add-on)
tiers.notes: Adds SAML/OIDC SSO, approvals workflow, and priority support with an 8-hour target response time. Activity-log retention 2 months; session-replay retention 12 months.

tiers.name: Enterprise (platform package)
tiers.notes: Page explicitly says "Custom pricing" with a "Talk to a human" CTA — no public number. Adds RBAC, property access control, SCIM provisioning, dedicated account manager; retention extends to 60 months for activity logs and session replay. Billing basis: contact_sales.

cons: Enterprise-grade security and governance controls are not covered by usage-based billing — they're gated behind separate flat platform packages: SSO enforcement and a HIPAA BAA require the $250/month Boost package, SAML/OIDC SSO requires the $750/month Scale package, and RBAC plus SCIM provisioning are only available on the Enterprise package, which has no public price and requires contacting sales.

Support responsiveness and data retention scale sharply with price tier rather than with usage: the $250/month Boost tier retains activity logs for only 7 days and states no support SLA at all, an 8-hour 'target' (not guaranteed) response time only starts at the $750/month Scale tier, and full 60-month retention plus a dedicated account manager require custom, contact-sales-only Enterprise pricing.

Total cost is hard to forecast because PostHog meters 13+ products independently (analytics events, session recordings, feature-flag requests, error-tracking exceptions, survey responses, data-warehouse rows, log GB, AI credits, etc.), each with its own free-tier ceiling and its own per-unit rate, rather than one simple flat or per-seat price.
